1.explanation: The heart of the problem lives in the hasPunctuatorBefore function in minification-estimator.js. Its PUNCTUATOR_REGEX does not include the keyword “case,” so when looking backward from a slash that follows ‘case’, the code never sees “case” as a valid punctuator. Instead, it assumes division and then sees ‘//’ as the start of a comment, causing the rest of the script to be ignored. Adding “case” to PUNCTUATOR_REGEX (as shown in the suggested diff) ensures regex literals after `case` are recognized correctly and prevents false unminified warnings.
1.bug_scenario: When Lighthouse’s Minify JavaScript audit runs against code containing a RegExp literal immediately after a “case” keyword (for example, switch(true){case/^hello!/.test("hello!"): ...}), the minification-estimator incorrectly treats the slash after “case” as the division operator rather than the start of a regex. It then misparses subsequent // as a comment, skips the rest of the code, and concludes the script is not minified—even though it is.

2.explanation: The only file that implements the logic for detecting whether a JavaScript file is minified is minification-estimator.js. It contains the PUNCTUATOR_REGEX used by hasPunctuatorBefore(), and this regex is missing “case” as a valid preceder to a RegExp literal. Adding “case” to that alternation fixes the misclassification. No other files participate in the minification‐detection logic, so only this file must be edited.
